# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 70/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16 ÷ 23 × 100 = 70. High = (16 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 70.

Every rule could be decided from the code, so the score is a single number. All results are read from code, not measured on a live site. I sampled 5 routes: `/`, `/pricing`, `/docs`, `/blog` and `/thank-you`. Four of them are in the sitemap and nav.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Point `robots.txt` at your sitemap
- **Why it matters:** the sitemap is your list of pages. Crawlers look in `robots.txt` to find it, and it doesn't mention it.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` (there is no `Sitemap:` line anywhere in the file)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 78/100. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml` (GEO-011).

### 2. Set the page language on `<html>`
- **Why it matters:** `lang` tells machines and screen readers which language the site is in. `geo.config.json` already says `en`, but the layout doesn't use it.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 78/100. Change it to `<html lang="en">` (GEO-012).

### 3. Give every indexable page one canonical link
- **Why it matters:** a canonical link names the main address of a page. `/docs` and `/blog` have none. `/pricing` has one but is marked noindex, so its canonical points at a page that tells search engines to stay away.
- **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1`, `app/blog/page.tsx`, `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 74/100 if you add canonicals to `/docs` and `/blog`. It reaches 78/100 if you also remove the noindex from `/pricing` (item below under GEO-014).

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and small | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`: valid lines, tiny file |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers can access the site | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` allows `*`. Only GPTBot (a training crawler) is blocked, which matches your policy |
| GEO-014 | Linked and sitemap pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/pricing` has `robots: { index: false }` (`app/pricing/page.tsx:1`). 3 of 4 routes are clear |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your domain | Problem | Not run | `/` is clear. `/docs` and `/blog` have none. `/pricing`'s canonical is noindex. 1 of 4 routes is clear |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `app/blog/page.tsx:7-9` loads posts in `useEffect`. 3 of 4 routes are clear |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD in the project |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid, but `robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:11` has no `lang`. Titles and descriptions are present on every route |
| GEO-016 | Pages reachable by plain links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:13`: `<a href>` links to all four main pages |
| GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | Not run | Only element-level `data-nosnippet` (`app/layout.tsx:15`). No middleware or headers config |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | I read `layout.tsx` and all five pages: no images, and the links have text |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | No `llms.txt` present. This isn't a problem |

## Other problems found

- **A noindex page is listed in the sitemap and nav:** `public/sitemap.xml:4`: `<loc>https://www.ledger.example/pricing</loc>`. The page itself says `robots: { index: false, follow: true }` (`app/pricing/page.tsx:1`). Either remove the noindex, if you want pricing found, or drop it from the sitemap and nav.

## Worth considering

- **The blog list is invisible to crawlers that don't run JavaScript:** `app/blog/page.tsx:8`: `fetch('/api/posts')`. This is the cause of the GEO-003 result. Loading posts on the server would put the titles in the HTML. Each post could also get its own page and address, which might help it be found.
- **Pricing details are thin:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:2`: `Free for up to three people.` A visitor would likely want to know what paid plans cost, and the page doesn't say. The meta description promises "Plans for every team size", and the page doesn't deliver that.
- **The docs page is a single sentence:** `app/docs/page.tsx:2`: `Start by importing your bank feed.` The description says "How to set up Ledger", but the page doesn't explain how to do it.
- **The company facts could be labelled with structured data:** `app/layout.tsx:5`: `title: 'Ledger: accounting for small teams'`. Organization or SoftwareApplication JSON-LD could label what the product is, if you want that.
- **Thin metadata on the home page:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Invoices, expenses and reports in one place.` The home page has no links onward to the product pages beyond the nav. A few lines linking to pricing and docs might help readers.
- **Sitemap dates:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `<url><loc>https://www.ledger.example/</loc></url>`. Add `<lastmod>` once you have real update dates.
- **Language setting isn't connected:** `geo.config.json` has `"language": "en"`, but nothing in the layout uses it. See item 2 above.

## Can't tell from code

- **GEO-013, GEO-014 and GEO-011:** the code doesn't show real status codes, redirects, `X-Robots-Tag` headers, or whether the sitemap URLs answer 200. A live scan with your site's URL would confirm them.
- **Blog posts:** the contents of `/api/posts` aren't in the repository.
- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. `geopilot logs <access log>` checks real crawlers against their published addresses.

## Assumptions

- You want search and AI search tools to find the site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.
- `/thank-you` is deliberately noindex and kept out of the sitemap, so I left it alone.
- `/pricing`'s noindex looks unintended because the page is in your nav and sitemap, but you may have a reason for it.
- Rendering is Next.js App Router, with the pages other than `/blog` as server components.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
